article_title: From Cognitive Outsourcing to Reallocation: A 3P Analysis of Student–Generative AI Engagement in Unsupervised Assessments
citation: Yan, W., Cui, Y., Chiu, T. K. F., Nakajima, T., & Kozima, H. (2026). From cognitive outsourcing to reallocation: A 3P analysis of student–generative AI engagement in unsupervised assessments. Australasian Journal of Educational Technology, 42(3), 41–61. https://doi.org/10.14742/ajet.11725
title: The 3P (presage-process-product) model operationalised for GenAI-supported assessment
description: The study applies Biggs' presage-process-product model to student–generative AI engagement in unsupervised higher-education assessments. It "operationalised and contextualised the 3P model in GenAI-supported assessment by articulating how presage factors shape distinct process patterns and perceived outcomes." Presage factors (intentions, contexts) are linked to process patterns of GenAI use and to perceived product outcomes, providing an explanatory framework for analysing human–GenAI collaboration in assessment.
requirements: Analysis requires data on students' GenAI usage intentions, dialogue patterns and integration with other learning activities in authentic assessment contexts
constraints: Developed and illustrated through qualitative analysis of undergraduates in Japan and China in after-class assessment contexts
target_learning_goals: cognitive engagement with generative AI in assessment tasks
examples: The study analysed 38 undergraduate students from Japan and China, examining their GenAI usage intentions, dialogue patterns and integration with other learning activities.
